s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent respiratory symptoms with acute exacerbation and severe ventilation dysfunction
salient_findings: Hyperresonance in percussion of both lungs
Loud and diffuse wheezing rales in both lungs
Low SpO2 and high respiratory rate
key_facts: 6-year history of recurrent respiratory symptoms
Acute exacerbation with dyspnea for 1 day
Hospitalization in ICU one year ago requiring mechanical ventilation for over 10 days
FEV1 PreD of 26% and FEV1/FVC percent of 56%
Asthma Control Test score of 9
Asthma Control Questionnaire score of 6
Vital signs: temperature 35.5°C, pulse 121 beats/min, respiratory rate 32 times/min, blood pressure 169/100 mmHg, SpO2 83%
Physical findings: orthopnea, cyanosis of the lips, profuse sweating, three-concave sign
Blood gas analysis: pH 7.137, PCO2 74.7 mmHg, PO2 95.0 mmHg, SO2 94.0%, FiO2 41.0%, oxygenation index 232 mmHg
Complete blood count: WBC 15.51 × 10^9/L, neutrophil percentage 74.2%, eosinophil percentage 7.2%
Chest CT: no major abnormalities observed in both lungs and heart
Bronchodilator test: increase in absolute FEV1 of 250 mL, improvement rate of 24%

shortlist.label: Asthma
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent respiratory symptoms, acute exacerbation, and positive response to bronchodilator test

shortlist.label: Status asthmaticus
shortlist.why_kept: Severe ventilation dysfunction, hyperresonance, and wheezing rales in both lungs

shortlist.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
shortlist.why_kept: Severe mixed ventilation dysfunction and history of hospitalization in ICU

shortlist.label: Cystic fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent respiratory symptoms and severe ventilation dysfunction, although less likely given age and lack of other typical symptoms

shortlist.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Severe hypoxemia, hypercapnia, and respiratory failure, although the chest CT shows no major abnormalities

raw.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent respiratory symptoms, acute exacerbation with dyspnea, and previous hospitalization requiring mechanical ventilation, along with the current vital signs and physical findings such as orthopnea, cyanosis, and wheezing, are consistent with a severe asthma exacerbation. The bronchodilator test showing an improvement in FEV1 also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Asthma
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of asthma, the current presentation with severe symptoms and respiratory failure is more consistent with status asthmaticus.

rejected.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of smoking history make COPD less likely, and the bronchodilator test results do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cystic fibrosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of symptoms or test results consistent with cystic fibrosis, such as recurrent infections or pancreatic insufficiency.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has hypoxemia and respiratory failure, the chest CT shows no major abnormalities, and the diagnosis of ARDS typically requires a known cause and bilateral infiltrates on chest imaging.

gold: Near-fatal asthma with type II respiratory failure and respiratory acidosis
